runs Upstream's script with a staging home and without the per-user scripts of install/user/all.sh (per-user setup ran those it allows); writes only its session and app files (the agent skill links), its default launchers with OnlyShowIn=Motanka; and its done marker through the User_Ledger, and drops the XDG user folders, GTK bookmarks and default applications it sets, which other sessions read
rewrites /boot/limine.conf
rewrites /etc/pacman.conf and the mirror list; 'sudo motanka doctor --fix' switches Motanka's apt suite
create exits 127, Upstream's code for "no snapshot tool", because 'sudo motanka update' takes Motanka's snapshot; restore is not available (use 'sudo motanka rollback') and exits 64
writes sudoers files, which Motanka never ships; --active reports inactive (exit 1) and --disable reports already disabled
reinstalls the system with Upstream's Arch installer

changes nothing and exits 0 (journal entry): Upstream writes the theme color as browser policy files under /etc through the unsupported omarchy-theme-set-browser-policy, which would end every theme switch with "Theme retint failed"
runs Upstream's script; drops --activate (from install/user/theme.sh) when ~/.config/fcitx5/conf/classicui.conf exists, so the Fcitx5 setting the user's other sessions read stays as it is
runs Upstream's script without --activate (from install/user/theme.sh): only the theme file is synced, and ~/.pi/agent/settings.json, which Pi reads in every session, is never written
runs 'sudo motanka update' (--yes for -y): Motanka's snapshot, the upgrade of the Motanka packages, the channel's Upstream pin and this user's pending migrations

checks that motanka-archive-keyring and its key file are installed; apt keeps the key current

prints the vendored Upstream version: the stable pin's release tag without its "v", else Upstream's version file; never calls pacman
